column1: management-plane|D|D1|crest|Why limit device-management access to designated administration paths?|Management services expose privileged control operations|Management protocols never require authentication|A VLAN name alone authenticates every administrator|The management IP determines all user-data encryption|Narrow reachability reduces attack exposure; authentication, privilege, and logging still need review.|A management plane deserves its own access policy.

snmp-context|D|D1|snmp|An SNMP credential reads one context but cannot read another. What should findings specify?|The principal, security level, and accessible context|Only that the device supports SNMP|Only the credential's character count|Only the routing protocol's metric|SNMP views and contexts can narrow access. A successful read does not establish complete device visibility or writes.|Management access can be scoped to a view.

span-limits|D|D2|crest|A switch mirror captures only one selected port. What is a limitation of the PCAP?|Traffic on unmirrored paths may be absent|All network traffic is guaranteed present|Every absent protocol is disabled globally|The capture automatically authenticates every payload|Collection topology defines visibility. Loss, selection, and timing also affect what the capture can show.|A capture is evidence from a collection point.

vlan-trunk|D|D3|crest|A trunk permits VLANs 10 and 20. What is its intended Layer 2 role?|Carry frames for those VLANs across the link|Route every packet to all subnets|Authenticate every connected user|Decrypt every wireless frame|Trunking transports several VLAN contexts. Inter-VLAN routing and user authentication are separate functions.|Carrying traffic is not granting every cross-VLAN path.

native-vlan|D|D3|crest|Why inspect the native VLAN on an 802.1Q trunk?|Untagged traffic may be assigned to that VLAN|It determines every certificate's issuer|It is always the same as a user's DNS suffix|It encrypts the switch's management password|Native-VLAN assumptions can affect tagging and isolation. Match both ends and review access/trunk configuration.|Untagged does not mean outside every VLAN context.

stp-root|D|D3|crest|Why can accepting a superior BPDU from an untrusted access port be dangerous?|It may change the chosen STP root and forwarding topology|It automatically reveals every WPA2 passphrase|It necessarily disables all TCP checksums|It turns every device into an SMTP relay|STP topology control can influence traffic paths. Guard features and port roles constrain who may influence it.|Control-plane messages can change data-plane behavior.

bpduguard-rootguard|D|D3|crest|Which distinction best describes BPDU Guard versus Root Guard?|Unexpected BPDUs versus superior-root claims are different trigger conditions|Both are identical names for ARP validation|Both encrypt Ethernet broadcasts|Both determine DHCP lease duration|Guard features address different topology-control conditions. Apply the feature matching the intended port role and threat.|Similar product names may protect different invariants.

dhcp-binding|D|D3|dhcp|Why can Dynamic ARP Inspection depend on DHCP snooping bindings?|Bindings provide a basis for validating claimed IP/MAC relationships|DHCP encrypts every ARP frame|An IP address alone proves host identity|Inspection can never support static address cases|Trusted binding data or explicit configuration supports validation. Static hosts and trusted ports need appropriate treatment.|Validation is only as good as its reference data.

hsrp-control|D|D3|crest|What does a first-hop redundancy virtual IP primarily provide?|A stable default-gateway address across router failover|A new independent authentication factor for every user|A certificate authority for all LAN services|A database replication endpoint|Routers can share a virtual gateway role. Protocol authentication and peer trust determine control-plane robustness.|Availability mechanisms can have their own trust boundaries.

vpn-fingerprint|D|D4|ipsec|An IKE responder returns proposal information. What is established before any authenticated tunnel exists?|A responsive negotiation endpoint and disclosed capabilities|Authorized access to every internal subnet|Possession of the pre-shared key|Successful decryption of application payloads|Negotiation can support fingerprinting. Tunnel authentication and traffic selectors are further boundaries.|Pre-authentication responsiveness is not internal access.

sip-register|D|D5|sip|What is SIP REGISTER principally used to update?|A user's contact-location binding at a registrar|The media stream's audio sample rate|The router's Ethernet forwarding table|A browser's HSTS list|Registration supports locating a user agent. Call setup and RTP media have different roles.|SIP methods express distinct signaling operations.

wifi-monitor-limit|D|D6|wifi|A monitor-mode adapter is listening on one channel. Why might it miss another AP's frames?|The other AP may transmit on a different channel or band|Monitor mode necessarily captures every band simultaneously|All APs share the same RF channel|The SSID alone selects the receiver frequency|Hardware, channel selection, band support, and timing determine capture visibility.|A capture mode does not imply unlimited RF coverage.
